_readme: Brand recognition per country for Heatpump Finder, owner decision 2026-11-06. A=5 stars, B=4, C=3, D=2, anything else 1. Recognition only, not quality, and regardless of who manufactures. Most placements are judgement from weak signals: evidence says how far each can be trusted. Review yearly, or when search-volume data becomes available. Used for ordering only and never sent to the browser.

LU.notes: Luxembourg does not credibly reach 40 brands: only about 17 have any direct Luxembourg source, so D is deliberately short (3). Everything below the first 17 entries is judgement from DE, BE or FR presence, and per the owner rule most brands fall to E. No market share, survey or national consumer test was found. GB.notes: No official brand data: I found no MCS, DESNZ, Ofgem or Nesta figures by manufacturer. The MCS dashboard would not load in my fetch and a third-party guide (poweringhomes.co.uk/statistics/mcs-data-dashboard/) lists its filters without manufacturer; the MCS Installations Database can be filtered by manufacturer but I could not get counts from it. I found no Which? brand ranking or owner survey, so its use here is the list of 19 companies it asked in July 2026 (Aira, Daikin, Grant, Ideal, LG, MasterTherm, Octopus, Samsung, Stiebel Eltron, Viessmann supplied data; Dimplex, Midea, NIBE, Panasonic, Vaillant did not respond; Baxi, Hitachi, Mitsubishi, Worcester Bosch could not answer). All 19 are in A or B. Which? installer counts are company-supplied, and Ideal shows 0. Euromonitor shows only its top two shares without a paid report. The Alchemy survey is published through Mitsubishi with no rival figures, so it is weak-to-medium. The Renewable Heating Hub poll (5,700 votes, Oct-Dec 2024) is an open vote that says it does not measure share. HeatpumpMonitor (859 public systems, downloaded Nov 2026, counted on hp_manufacturer, mostly air source) is an enthusiast sample tilted towards installers who publish data, and Heat Geek fits Vaillant; it is a signal of who is known and installed, not of share. Referral and brand-comparison sites were treated as weak, and I did not use their share tables. One I opened, hetapro.com, was not used: as read, it wrongly places Worcester Bosch under Vaillant. heatable.co.uk and glowgreenltd.com refused my fetch and are not cited. No tier is rated strong because none rests on official data. A is judgement at the edges: Mitsubishi, Daikin and Vaillant are the best supported, while NIBE, Panasonic, LG, Aira and Baxi are within judgement of each other. Below B almost all placement is judgement, and C and D are close to interchangeable. pelListings counts ASHP (air-to-water) rows in the 2026-11 PEL, summed across a brand's legal names; it counts listings, not sales. Examples of summing: Mitsubishi 40 (Mitsubishi plus Mitsubishi Electric Air Conditioning Systems Europe, excludes Heavy Industries), Samsung 227, Hitachi 248 and Hisense 25 both include 19 Qingdao Hisense Hitachi rows, Grant 25 (UK plus Ireland), Viessmann 146. Glow Worm's 3 are GeniaAir rows filed under Vaillant Group UK Ltd, so they are also inside Vaillant's 34. Catalogue traps: ALPHA INNOTEC (58 cards, ait-deutschland) is not the UK's Alpha Innovation; Buderus (162), Saunier Duval (97; saunierduval.co.uk is a domain for sale) and ROTEX have many cards but no UK presence that I found, so they stay E; ORCA_MITSUBISHI_ELECTRIC (28 cards) is a data-label variant of Mitsubishi and should be merged or it will score E; catalogue Mitsubishi model names do not contain Ecodan and Bosch ones do not contain Worcester, so a UK reader may not recognise them. Grant, Ideal and Aira are now present but thin (5, 6 and 4 cards). Missing from the catalogue: Octopus Energy (Cosy), tiered A with inCatalogue false, is the only missing brand I consider truly well known. Not tiered because they are not well known enough to take a slot, but worth adding: Trianco (14 PEL rows under TR Engineering, sold through EDF per Which?, would be C), Alpha Innovation (5 PEL rows, UK boiler brand with heat pumps at alpha-innovation.co.uk, would be C or D), Ebac (2 PEL rows, UK-made, ebac.com/heatpumps, would be D), Global Energy Systems (12 PEL rows, 2 HeatpumpMonitor systems, named in Renewable Heating Hub's community list, would be D). Kensa (kensa.co.uk) is ground source only, with 34 PEL rows all WSHP and none ASHP, and is well known for that, so it is out of an air-to-water list. Heatrae Sadia (heatraesadia.com, Baxi group) makes cylinders and hot water products: no heat pump content on its home page, no PEL rows and no catalogue cards, so it is not tiered. British Gas, EDF, E.ON and Scottish Power install other makers' units and are not product brands. I found nothing on national advertising, sponsorship or UK revenue by brand, so those signals did not move any placement. Placement of LG and every other brand used the same evidence; no placement used the owner's employer in either direction.

BE.notes: No published Belgian sales ranking, Test-Achats/Test-Aankoop brand test or Bouwkroniek survey was found; the Test-Achats dossier I opened names no brands. Belgian evidence is commercial comparison and lead-generation sites plus the Belgian heat pump association platform (InfoWarmtePomp), whose 39-name list only shows presence, not size. Hence medium at best. Bulex is the main Belgium-specific result: it is barely visible in other markets but sits in A here. I found no Flanders vs Wallonia split in the data; Bulex, Atlantic, De Dietrich and Thermor probably read stronger in Wallonia, but that is my inference. PL.notes: Poland has the weakest current evidence of the three: the only brand recognition survey found dates from end 2008 and the only share tables from 2007 and 2010, before the air-water boom. PORT PC and SPIUG publish no per-brand shares. No A placement is strong; the current mix comes from guides that are commercial and unscored. Daikin's president claimed in 2024 that Polish IGU OZE members hold 2% of the market, a competitor's unsourced assertion, which is one reason local makers sit low despite good awareness. Kospel, Kaisai, Rotenso and Galmet may deserve different tiers if distributor data appears. rotex.pl is an unrelated plastics firm, so ROTEX was not placed despite PORT PC listing a Rotex logo. Hitachi was not placed because no Polish evidence loaded. SilesiaTERM and Kołton (Oferteo) just missed D. Sites that did not load are inconclusive.
